newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-TOGO LEAD WAY INTO NATIONS CUP FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TOGO LEAD WAY INTO NATIONS CUP FINALS.

text.p: Togo led the charge of qualifiers for next year's African Nations Cup finals with a one-sided 4-0 win over Liberia on Sunday as four other countries also booked their places in Burkina Faso.
Togo qualfied for the biennial tournament for the first time since 1984 and will be joined by Cameroon, Ghana, Morocco and Zambia who all won their matches at the weekend.

Tadjou Salou, who plays club soccer in Switzerland, set the Togolese on their way at the Municipal stadium in Lome with a 52nd minute strike and a barrage of three goals in the last four minutes sealed a famous win.
Kossi Noutsoudje, Komlan Assignon and fittingly Bachirou Salou, the German-based king-pin of their qualifying campaign, all grabbed late goals to secure top place in group six.
Cameroon's qualification was finalised on Sunday afternoon, 24 hours after they had won 1-0 in Namibia with a 69th minute goal by Joseph Tchango.
Gabon's 1-0 win over Kenya in Libreville means that Cameroon will fill one of the two qualifying places in group five, even if they are beaten in their final match at home to Kenya in two weeks.

Salaheddine Bassir scored a second successive winning goal for Morocco to put them through from group three. His 21st-minute strike against Ethiopia in Addis Ababa saw Morocco qualify for the first time since the 1992 tournament.
Three-time African Footballer of the Year Abedi Pele set up Ghana's progress to the finals with the opening goal against Zimbabwe in Accra on Sunday.
Although his goal was quickly cancelled out by Zimbabwean midfielder Shephard Muradzikwa, Ghana secured a 2-1 victory with Osei Kuffour's 39th minute winner.
Zimbabwe can still take second place in group one if they avoid defeat against Angola in Luanda on July 27.

Zambia became the first side to qualify on Saturday with an effortless 3-1 win over neigbours Malawi, set up with a first-half penalty by Hector Chilombo and second-half goals from Frazer Kamwandi and Freddie Mwila junior.
Zambia were playing without all but one of their foreign-based professionals, who ignored a call-up for the game from coach George Mungwa.
Malawi needed only a draw to qualify but coach Ruben Malola blamed a sloppy midfield for the defeat. "We lost concentration," he said.
Former Nations Cup winners Algeria and Egypt kept up their late bids to go through with home wins against teams who need just a point to qualify.

Egypt beat Senegal 2-0 in Cairo on Sunday night, inspired by the return to action of Hazem Imam, while Algeria laboured to a 1-0 win over Mali on Friday. Both can qualify with home wins in their final matches on July 27.
But 1992 winners Ivory Coast wasted an opportunity to secure their place, drawing 0-0 away against minnows Benin when a win would have seen them through.
The nine outstanding places will be decided on the weekend of July 26-27 when the final round of qualifiers are played.
